preamble: The alveolar nasal /n/ is realized as a voiced uvular nasal [ɴ] chiefly through regressive place assimilation to a following uvular consonant: syllable-final /n/ copies the place of a following /q/ or /χ/. This is a regular allophonic process in Quechua before /q/ and in Castilian Spanish before uvular /x/ ([χ]). Japanese shows a different, prosodically conditioned case: the moraic nasal is realized as [ɴ] utterance-finally, although it is usually analysed as a placeless archiphoneme /N/ rather than /n/.

examples.note: Before the uvular stop /q/ the nasal assimilates to uvular place; the uvular also lowers the surrounding high vowels to [ɔ o].
Syllable-final /n/ takes the place of the following consonant; in northern and central Spain /x/ is uvular [χ], so the nasal surfaces as [ɴ].
Utterance-finally the moraic nasal is realized as uvular [ɴ]; before consonants it assimilates in place instead.

context: Before uvular consonants (/q/, /χ/); utterance-finally for the Japanese moraic nasal
